summary: Iteration 16 end-to-end verification of the disp-1.4.0 changes on the deployed preview. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration16.py (23 tests, all pass) plus a full playwright pass on sample.reader's four result pages, /mirrors and /methodology. All 189 local guard tests in /app/tests also pass. The five requested behaviours were verified: (Q1) elevation and shadow basis print on the essential result page (data-testid essential-elevation and essential-shadow-basis both present; delta payload carries elevation, elevation_share, centred_per_archetype and stamps display_version disp-1.4.0; centred/ipsatised never surface in reader-facing copy); (Q2) EI named block returns mrd 0.765 (docstring says 0.764 - one-ulp rounding drift, see nit below) with assumed_alpha 0.70; sample.reader's four domains span 0.36 so highest/lowest are null, the flat_copy 'within measurement error' renders under eq-named-flat, the facet_note under eq-facet-note, no 'Leading with' / 'Worth developing' ranked lists appear; (Q3) 'most reliable thing' is absent from every result JSON, from /mirrors and from every rendered result page and combined PDF; cross-check cards declare polarity per reading and their bodies read 'inherits the weaker of the two instruments it is built from, not the stronger'; (Q4) sd_flag() cuts at 7 and 9 - the frontend re-derives from agree_count using the new cuts, so sample.reader's stored count of 4 renders NORMAL and no warning banner appears (the choosing block also stays silent below HIGH); (Q5) speeding is exposed as items_timed / below_floor / below_floor_pct with a 300 ms/word floor - no bare mean is reported. Cross-check emission path was exercised on the three deliberate accounts: set1e (all-middle) produces only 'Nothing to report' cards - no 'Agreement' card fires; set2e / set3e together produce at least one real agreement or tension card, and every emitted convergence/tension card carries evidence_tier and confidence and prints the 'inherits the weaker' caveat. Synthesis rules on sample.reader hold: 'How you choose - the short version' does NOT claim what the selection 'runs on' (Closeness is Low confidence and mid-range), names 'Personality Mirror' explicitly when citing a trait, and prints 'sit too close together to name one' for the flat EI domains. /methodology loads and contains both new paragraphs. Combined PDF is 200 %PDF and > 20 KB; every individual instrument PDF renders. Ownership enforcement holds - ui.demo receives 403/404 on all five sample.reader session ids. Registration/login regression passes; Junction anonymous flow passes.

ui_bugs.issue: frontend/src/content/situationFraming.js line 8 still ships the dated forecast phrase 'The gap below is a prediction, not a post-mortem'. This text renders on the essential result page for any single_dating reader (verified on sample.reader). Iteration 16 spec explicitly forbids 'prediction rather than a post-mortem'.

Spec: 'an agree_count of 4 ... now reads normal WITH THE CHANCE-LEVEL NOTE'. Current code (PersonalityResult.js line 64) gates the entire note behind sd !== 'NORMAL', so at count 4 no chance-level note is shown at all. The best-self warning is correctly hidden; the neutral chance-level note is also missing.

miLearn.js lines 24, 53, 145 still carry 'at about week six' / 'at week six' shadow-attraction forecasts, and line 142-143 still uses 'the post-mortem'. If Learn articles are considered reader-facing (they are public), these phrases need the same treatment as the result-page copy. Not currently displayed on any result page or PDF.

action_items: HIGH: remove or rephrase 'prediction, not a post-mortem' in frontend/src/content/situationFraming.js single_dating essential framing - it prints on every single-dating reader's essential result page (sample.reader confirmed).

MEDIUM: PersonalityResult.js - show a neutral 'about four is what content-blind answering produces' chance-level note when agree_count is present (even at NORMAL); the current gate hides the note when sd==='NORMAL'.
LOW: sweep frontend/src/content/miLearn.js for 'week six' / 'post-mortem' if Learn articles are in scope.

NIT: services/reportable.py line 36 comment says 'EI_DOMAIN_MRD = mrd(EI_DOMAIN_SD) # 0.764 on the 1-5 scale' but the actual value is 0.765; update the comment (or reset the constant) so future test authors don't chase phantom drift.
critical_code_review_comments: _tier_and_confidence in crosscheck.py correctly returns the LOWER tier and LOWER confidence of the two inputs, using min() over rank dicts. The 'inherits the weaker' string is welded onto the caveat, so every agreement/tension body carries the caveat by construction rather than by convention. Good.

ei_named() gates highest and lowest independently against the NEXT domain (not the mean). That is the correct floor: a score can sit well above the average of four and still be indistinguishable from the domain directly below it.

_elevation() carries centred_per_archetype into the payload but no reader-facing surface (choosing points, result page, PDF) prints it - the queued rk-1.1.0 change is respected. Verified by scanning choosing points for 'centred'/'ipsatised' on the sample.reader essential result.

The write-once snapshot rule is respected on the Personality validity flag: stored 'flag' still reads ELEVATED at count=4 because it was minted under the old cut, but PersonalityResult.js and the choosing block both re-derive from agree_count using the new cuts (9, 7). This is the right pattern - never edit a delivered snapshot; re-derive at read time.
One-ulp drift: reportable.mrd(0.60, 0.70) rounds to 0.765 while the inline comment claims 0.764. Trivial but worth aligning.

The cross-check emission path was correctly exercised only on set2e/set3e in this iteration - sample.reader's machine-generated mid-scale responses cannot distinguish a working gate from a broken one that suppresses everything. Future testing agents should retain those three fixtures.

context_for_next_testing_agent: disp-1.4.0 is live. Verified through backend JSON + frontend rendering + PDFs on the deployed preview. Key open item is the 'prediction rather than a post-mortem' string still in situationFraming.js (single_dating essential framing) - once that is fixed, retest the essential result page for sample.reader (and ideally set2e whose situation is also single_dating) and check that 'post-mortem' is absent. The three deliberate accounts (set1e/set2e/set3e) are the ONLY way to exercise the cross-check emission path - sample.reader is machine-generated mid-scale and will always produce nulls. TIE_MARGIN=5 essential tie state remains regression-critical.
rca of the issue: 'prediction, not a post-mortem' leak: situationFraming.js is a plain frontend content module imported at runtime (not snapshotted), so a single line edit will remove it everywhere in one deploy. Reproduction: log in as sample.reader (single_dating), open /results/3f8f2b03-2bb1-4e39-a710-2b89ff6c5851, search the page HTML for 'post-mortem'. Mitigation: rewrite the sentence to drop the dated-forecast framing (e.g. keep the 'shadow arriving as chemistry' clause, drop the 'prediction, not a post-mortem' hinge). Chance-level note gap: PersonalityResult.js line 64 - split the note into two: an always-shown neutral 'about four is what content-blind answering produces' whenever agree_count is present, and the extra 'best-self version, take it again' warning only when sd !== 'NORMAL'.
